title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-noah-v2
content:
Goal: capture repro steps, commands tried, observed errors, hypotheses, and next experiments for intermittent SSE / chunked streaming issues (client-side truncation and large-response stalls).

Context / symptom summary:
- Intermittent reports from a handful of customers where long-form streaming responses (SSE / chunked) stop delivering events after ~10-30s or deliver big pauses. Frontend sees stream 'hang' or partial last event.
- Repro is flaky locally but consistent under load or with particular middleboxes (nginx proxy + gzip + HTTP/1.1).
- Errors in upstream logs vary: sometimes no error (client closed), sometimes 502 upstream prematurely closed connection, sometimes Node emits \"Error: write EPIPE\" or \"ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED\".

Quick notes / mental model:
- Two behavior buckets: (A) chunking/flush not propagating all the way through proxy (buffering), (B) backpressure in node writable stream leading to dropped data when socket aborts mid-stream.
- Common culprits: proxy buffering (nginx/ALB), gzip compression delay, Node highWaterMark and not waiting for 'drain', client aborts (browser nav, network flakiness) causing EPIPE.

Repro commands I ran (local):
1) Simple SSE with curl -N to keep connection open:
   # server running on localhost:3000 (below)
   curl -v -N http://localhost:3000/stream?sleep=50

2) Observe chunking raw TCP with netcat (to ensure transfer-encoding chunks present):
   curl -sN http://localhost:3000/stream?sleep=10 | nc -l 9999
   # Then connect with telnet to inspect bytes: telnet localhost 9999

3) Test through nginx (local config) to reproduce buffering behavior:
   # start nginx with local conf that proxies /stream to localhost:3000
   curl -v -N http://localhost:8080/stream?sleep=20

4) Python streaming client (requests) to see behavior programmatically:
   import requests
   r = requests.get('http://localhost:8080/stream?sleep=30', stream=True)
   for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
       print('LINE:', line)

Observed outputs / error snippets (collected):
- Node server stdout:
  [2025-02-14T14:21:12Z] connection start
  [2025-02-14T14:21:22Z] wrote event #5 (res.write OK)
  [2025-02-14T14:21:25Z] write returned false -> backpressure
  [2025-02-14T14:21:25Z] socket closed by client (ECONNRESET)
  [2025-02-14T14:21:25Z] Error: write EPIPE

- nginx error.log (when it fails):
  2025/02/14 14:21:25 [error] 12345#0: *987 recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.5, server: _, request: "GET /stream?sleep=30 HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/stream?sleep=30", host: "localhost:8080"

- Browser console: no explicit errors; fetch abort shows in app-level code: \"TypeError: Failed to fetch\" when nav or network glitch.

Server code (minimal repro used locally):
- Node/Express SSE prototype (used to reproduce backpressure):
  const express = require('express')
  const app = express()
  app.get('/stream', (req,res) => {
    res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream')
    res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache')
    res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive')
    res.flushHeaders()
    let i = 0
    const t = setInterval(() => {
      const ok = res.write(`data: {\"i\":${i}}\\n\\n`)
      const ts = new Date().toISOString()
      console.log(`${ts} wrote event #${i} (res.write ${ok ? 'OK' : 'PAUSED'})`)
      i++
      if (i>200) { clearInterval(t); res.end(); }
      if (!ok) {
        // we're seeing this path in failing runs
        console.log('write returned false -> waiting for drain')
        res.once('drain', () => console.log('drain emitted - continue'))
      }
    }, 200)
  })
  app.listen(3000)

Experiments & results:
- Experiment A: proxy_buffering off + proxy_http_version 1.1 + chunked_transfer_encoding on in nginx
  - Result: much better; chunks arrive to curl immediately and Python client sees lines as they come.
  - But still observed occasional \"write returned false\" followed by socket close.

- Experiment B: disabled gzip on upstream paths (gzip off / gzip_proxied off)
  - Result: fewer large pauses (gzip was buffering to create larger compressed blocks).

- Experiment C: increase Node writable highWaterMark for socket to 32KB (experiment)
  - Result: changed frequency but not eliminated pauses under heavy load.

- Experiment D: flush after every write (res.flushHeaders + res.flush()) using compression middleware toggles
  - Result: helps but expensive; not ideal for production perf on high concurrency.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) nginx / proxy buffering + gzip combination is the dominant cause for observed pauses/truncation. Nginx collects small chunks to recompress/packetize leading to larger pauses; disabling proxy buffering and gzip reduces symptoms.
2) Node backpressure path: when res.write returns false we must wait for 'drain' before continuing. Our current code ignores false in some codepaths (legacy helper) leading to fast loop and potential socket errors when clients abort mid-write.
3) Client-side: some HTTP clients (mobile/older browsers) aggressively close sockets on transient cellular blips; server doesn't handle clean drain -> abrupt socket close -> EPIPE.
4) ALB / managed load balancer timeouts (idle timeout) can drop streaming connections if keep-alive / keepalive pings not present.

Immediate fixes to try (in order):
- Ensure nginx conf uses proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection \"\"; proxy_request_buffering off; set \"X-Accel-Buffering: no\" header for upstreams.
- Disable gzip for SSE endpoints (we already tested: helps).
- Audit server code to ALWAYS honor res.write(...) returning false. Add a small queue and pause sending until drain event. Avoid tight intervals that continue writes when backpressure reported.
- Add periodic keep-alive comment events (\": keepalive\\n\\n\") every 15s to prevent idle timeouts in ALBs.
- Add extra logging to capture bytesWritten counters and timestamps to find exact gap durations.

Potential longer-term mitigations:
- Move SSE endpoints to a dedicated workers pool with tuned socket buffer sizes and fewer middleboxes.
- Implement HTTP/2 server push or grpc-streaming alternative (requires client changes).
- Add server-side per-connection buffer accounting and shed load gracefully when per-connection buffers exceed threshold.

Next experiments to run (TODOs):
- [ ] Run a consistent load test through nginx with proxy_buffering toggled and measure time-to-first-byte and average inter-event latency. Use vegeta or wrk with a simple SSE consumer (custom client) that measures inter-chunk gaps.
- [ ] Write small harness that simulates poor network: drop packets / random short disconnects to simulate mobile to reproduce EPIPE vs graceful close.
- [ ] Instrument server to export a metric: \"sse_backpressure_events_per_minute\" when res.write returns false. Add to console logs + Prometheus.
- [ ] Add more robust client-side reconnection logic (exponential backoff + resume) for partial streams.

Repro commands to automate (to add to repo/test-harness):
- start node server: NODE_ENV=dev node sse-demo.js
- start nginx (local) with conf in infra/nginx/sse-proxy.conf -> docker-compose up nginx
- run streaming client measurement script: python3 tools/stream_latency_measure.py --url http://localhost:8080/stream?sleep=60 --interval 0.2 --out results.json

Notes / small findings:
- curl -N shows chunks fine when connecting directly to node (no nginx). When nginx in front, default conf re-buffers -> all events appear as a big chunk. Setting \"proxy_buffering off\" made curl show streaming again.
- Some managed cloud LB (ALB) still reassembles and occasionally times out if last byte > idle_timeout. Keepalives are important.
- res.write returning false is the most reliable local indicator we hit backpressure. Don't ignore it.

Logs / sample timestamps from a failing scenario:
  2025-02-14T14:21:12Z client connect id=a1b2
  2025-02-14T14:21:13Z wrote event #1
  2025-02-14T14:21:14Z wrote event #2
  2025-02-14T14:21:18Z wrote event #6
  2025-02-14T14:21:18Z write returned false -> backpressure
  2025-02-14T14:21:25Z socket closed by client (ECONNRESET)
  2025-02-14T14:21:25Z Error: write EPIPE

Questions for the team / things to ask infra/GW owners:
- Do ALB / GCP LB / CloudFront preserve chunked transfer and SSE semantics? Any known issues with gzip enabled?
- What are our idle timeout defaults on prod LB? Can we support sending keepalive comments every 15-20s safely?
- Any intermediary (API gateway) that performs response buffering/compression? Confirm for enterprise customers that have inline WAFs.

References/notes from web:
- nginx SSE best-practices: set proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection \"\"; proxy_request_buffering off.
- Node backpressure docs: writable.write returns false -> wait for drain. Avoid busy loops.

Personal TODO (next 48h):
- Implement instrumentation for res.write returning false and add Prom alert if > 10/min per node.
- Create small reproducible test (wrk + custom SSE client) and run across staging with/without gzip and with proxy_buffering toggles.
- Draft short runbook for SSE endpoints: nginx config snippet + recommended Node pattern (honor write false, keepalive comments, disable gzip).

-- end notes --
